meta.name: Boriken Reconstruction Grammar
meta.word_order: SVO (learner-friendly Neo-Taíno only; classical word order is poorly attested and may have been freer / SOV-leaning)
meta.accuracy_note: Do not present SVO or reconstructed sentences as proven Classical Taíno. Prefer the six colonial spoken anchors when teaching historical structure. See ACCURACY.md.

notes: Flap [ɾ] was likely an allophone of /d/ (word-initial /d/, intervocalic /r/).
No onset consonant clusters; syllable-final consonant usually /s/ (plus masculine -el).
Stress usually penultimate, unless word ends in /e/, /i/, or a nasal vowel.

orthography_map.sh: x or ch in older Spanish transcriptions
orthography_map.h: h or j or x depending on scribe

verbal_prefixes.note: Subject marking on verbs often mirrors possessive prefixes.

overview.english: Neo-Taíno Boriken for learners usually follows Subject–Verb–Object (SVO) as a teaching default—not a proven Classical Taíno word order. Person is often marked on the verb with the same prefixes used for possession (da-/wa-/li-/to-). Identity sentences use daka ('I am'), which is colonially attested.
overview.spanish: El boriken neo-taíno para aprendices suele seguir Sujeto–Verbo–Objeto (SVO) como valor pedagógico—no como orden clásico demostrado. La persona se marca en el verbo con los mismos prefijos de posesión (da-/wa-/li-/to-). Las oraciones de identidad usan daka ('yo soy'), forma atestiguada en crónicas.

slot_guide.how: Use an independent noun/pronoun, OR mark person on the verb with da-/wa-/li-/to-.
Place the verb stem after the subject prefix: da-sá, wa-aka, li-arika.
Follows the verb in SVO order. May be bare or possessed.
Use ma- on a stem for 'without/not', or set phrases like mayani / makabuka.
Name/title after a comma in commands.

build_order: 1. Choose the sentence type (identity, action, possession, negation, command, hortative).
3. Attach the verb or noun stem.
4. Add object / complement in SVO order.
5. Label attestation: attested vs reconstructed composition.

reconstruction_rules.rule: Prefer attested colonial forms when available; mark confidence high.
If no attested form, propose from Ta-Arawakan cognates (Lokono, Garifuna, Wayuu) and label confidence low/medium.
Adapt candidate forms to Taíno phonotactics: CV syllables, no onset clusters, map foreign sounds.
Spanish loans historically adapted (espada→isúbara, espejo→isíbuse); apply similar adaptation for modern needed terms.
Always expose attestation status and rationale to the learner / app UI.
Default learner sentence order is SVO unless teaching an attested historical string.
Never upgrade community_revival or caribbean_spanish_uncertain forms to attested without a colonial citation. Expose ACCURACY.md /accuracy_note to learners.
Classical Taíno syntax is sparsely attested; do not claim SVO (or any fixed order) as historical fact.
